verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly offers automation-like primitives — scheduled flag changes, guarded rollouts (which autonomously monitor metrics and roll back), adaptive triggers, and webhooks — that can run without a human present, and its MCP server/CLI let an AI agent configure these. However, there is no evidence of a purpose-built 'autonomous agent' or background job orchestration framework tailored to AI-native workflows; the evidence is scattered across generic release-management docs rather than a coherent automation/agent story. Missing for 10: explicit AI-agent automation workflows, evidence of persistent background agent execution, and independent confirmation these features work as autonomous 'set and forget' automations.
